subject: MAP: Benchmark reconciliation checklist and close milestones
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Benchmark reconciliation checklist and close milestones

Hi Alice —

Following our demo last week, I pulled together a short reconciliation checklist so we can align MAP milestones with a final performance acceptance window. The goal: get to a go/no-go decision for Dedicated capacity by the end of week 2 of our MAP.

High-level asks from Acme for acceptance:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) < 120ms p50 on target request shapes
- Sustained throughput: 4000 tokens/sec for the canonical multi-turn flow at 8 concurrent sessions
- Concurrency: linear degradation no worse than 25% at 16 concurrent sessions

Proposed reconciliation checklist (attached as acme_map_v3.xlsx):
1) Run Redwood-hosted benchmark using MAP prompt set (attached CSV) — reproduce our numbers and capture per-token breakdowns. (Owner: Karthik)
2) Customer-local repro — Acme to run the same prompts from their staging VPC using our repro-instructions.md, send raw traces and KV-cache profiles. (Owner: Acme)
3) Tooling diff analysis — compare tokenization, request padding, and client-side batching between Acme harness and Redwood harness; identify differences that could explain 10-40% delta. (Owner: Marissa)
4) Competitive baseline check — run 1-shot A/B against their incumbent provider for identical prompt shapes and report latency/TTFT. (Owner: Rishi)
5) Final MAP milestone: mutual sign-off on methodology and results -> trigger Dedicated capacity order.

Can you confirm the owners on your side for step 2 and whether the Acme harness can produce KV cache dumps? If they can’t, we’ll provide a small instrumented client that spits out the same traces.

I’ve attached an initial results CSV from our hosted run — this is the run we want to reconcile to.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_map_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), benchmark-results-20261026.csv (CSV)

Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmark reconciliation checklist and close milestones

Alice —
Posting quick notes on tooling differences that often explain 10-30% deltas: tokenization inconsistencies (padding/off-by-one tokens), client-side pre/post-processing delays, and different keep-alive/socket reuse settings on the client.

Our hosted run used:
- Redwood tokenizer v2.4 with aggressive truncation rules (attached repro-instructions.md)
- Persistent HTTP/2 connections with connection pool size 16
- Server-side KV warmup between runs to avoid cold-cache TTFT spikes

If your staging harness doesn't reuse connections or warm the cache, TTFT numbers will look worse. We can ship a small instrumented client that mirrors our connection and batching behavior — it takes ~1 hour to integrate.

Proposed timeline:
- Oct 24: Redwood sends instrumented client + repro instructions (Karthik)
- Oct 25-26: Acme runs staging suite and returns traces + netcat-style token logs (Bryan)
- Oct 27: Redwood performs tooling-diff analysis and competitive baseline (Marissa/Rishi)
- Oct 28: Joint results call, decision on Dedicated capacity (All)

I'll attach a short checklist for what we need in the traces (timestamps for request start, first-token, per-token deltas, connection reuse flags).

-Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: repro-instructions.md

Marissa / Karthik —
Per plan we ran the staging suite yesterday and attached the raw traces (summaries below). Quick summary:
- p50 TTFT: 135ms; p90 TTFT: 240ms (our staging harness, no KV dumps yet)
- Sustained throughput observed: 3200 tokens/sec at 8 sessions, dropping to ~2500 at 16 sessions
- Connection reuse: the harness created new connections per test case by default (we'll flip to keep-alive and re-run if that is the recommended config)

I've uploaded the full trace bundle to our shared Drive and linked it in the MAP spreadsheet. We can run the instrumented client next if that will unblock regression analysis.

Thanks,
Bryan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Alice Park <alice@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmark reconciliation checklist and close milestones

Team —
We completed the tooling-diff and competitive baseline this morning. Key findings summarised:
1) Connection reuse accounted for ~22% of the TTFT gap. When we re-ran Redwood-hosted tests with new-connections-per-request, TTFT rose from 110ms to ~135ms, matching Acme's p50.
2) Tokenization mismatch (Acme's staging harness used an older tokenizer with different normalization rules) added ~8-12% on per-token latency due to extra token counts on canonical prompts.
3) Competitive baseline (incumbent provider) measured p50 TTFT ~160ms and throughput ~2800 tokens/sec for the canonical flow (with their standard keep-alive settings).

Actionable recommendations:
- Acme flips staging harness to persistent HTTP/2 and re-runs the suite (Owner: Bryan) — target complete by Oct 30 EOD.
- Redwood will supply an instrumented client and a short patch to normalize tokenization during the run so both sides are using v2.4 token rules (Owner: Karthik/Marissa) — delivery by Oct 29 morning.
- If re-run results align within 10% of Redwood-hosted numbers, we mark benchmarking acceptance complete and proceed with the Dedicated capacity procurement step.

I've uploaded a reconciliation checklist and a short annotated runbook to the MAP sheet. Let's keep the Oct 28 joint call on the calendar and convert to a quick close call if the re-run finishes earlier.

-Rishi
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
